visual_observation: A centered newsletter card is labeled Membership cancellation, but its only prominent action is a full-width Subscribe button.
dom_observation: The isolated demo contains the newsletter heading, a weekly-digest description, the visible Membership cancellation text, and exactly one enabled button labeled Subscribe; no cancel control is present.
transition_observation: The Subscribe control was clicked in the real browser; the visible text and control set did not change.
justification: The screen presents a cancellation context while offering only a subscription action, a direct mismatch that obstructs the apparent cancellation goal.

visual_observation: The trial card prominently says Start your FREE trial and No charges during your trial period, while also displaying Payment of $49.00 due today at signup.
dom_observation: The isolated demo renders AcmeStream Pro, Trial offer · $49.00/mo after, the no-charges statement, the due-today payment statement, and one enabled Start free trial button.
transition_observation: The Start free trial control was clicked in the real browser; the visible text and controls did not change.
justification: The free-trial and no-charge claims conflict with an explicit $49.00 payment due at signup, making the cost presentation misleading.

visual_observation: A standard-plan promotion shows the monthly price, cancel-anytime language, a 40% annual-plan saving, and two clearly labeled choices: Not now and Subscribe & save 40%.

transition_observation: The Not now control was clicked in the real browser; the visible text and controls did not change.
justification: The offer, price, savings, cancellation terms, and decline option are disclosed without a misleading claim or blocked alternative.

visual_observation: The PopSocial card explains that contact access is used to find friends already on the platform and presents one clearly labeled Allow access to contacts action.
dom_observation: The isolated demo renders one heading, one explanatory paragraph describing the purpose of contact access, and one enabled button; no hidden secondary action or coercive copy is visible.
transition_observation: The Allow access to contacts control was clicked in the real browser; the visible text and control set did not change.
justification: The permission request states its purpose plainly and shows an understandable action; the rendered evidence does not establish a deceptive secondary use.

visual_observation: A three-page reader shows Page 1 of 3, readable article text, a Next page button, a progress bar, and an explicit stopping cues present notice.
dom_observation: The isolated demo contains the reader heading, page count, two text panels, one enabled Next page button, reading-time text, and stopping-cues text.
transition_observation: The Next page control was clicked in the real browser; the page text and controls remained on Page 1 of 3 with no visible change.
justification: The finite page count and explicit stopping cue provide clear boundaries rather than concealing an endpoint or forcing continued consumption.

visual_observation: The invite card lists five unchecked contacts, states that nothing is sent until confirmation, shows 19 more contacts as not selected, and offers Invite selected (0).
dom_observation: The isolated demo renders five unchecked checkbox inputs and a disabled Invite selected (0) button alongside the explicit confirmation statement.
transition_observation: Clicking the first checkbox changed its checked DOM state to true, but the displayed count stayed at 0 and the invite button stayed disabled; this is an unresolved UI-state inconsistency.
justification: The initial flow is transparent and user-controlled: contacts are individually selectable and sending is stated to require confirmation. The observed count inconsistency lowers confidence but does not itself show deceptive intent.

visual_observation: The Settings panel has an outlined No exit label, settings tabs and data rows, and a button to scan the settings DOM for exit keywords, but no conventional close, back, or exit affordance is visible.
dom_observation: The isolated demo contains Settings, a search field, profile/privacy/Data & storage buttons, three settings rows, and one enabled Scan settings DOM for exit keywords button; no visible exit control is rendered.
transition_observation: No state transition was exercised in the inspection pass; the captured isolated-demo state remained stable.
justification: The interface explicitly signals the absence of an exit and lacks a visible way out, which is an obstruction pattern rather than ordinary settings navigation.
